content: 1. How have existing community structures and networks been involved in the planning, decision-making, and implementation of quality improvement activities at the health facility level? 2. What has been the extent of community engagement in improving the quality of services provided in health facilities? 3. What role should the community play in achieving better quality of care? 4. What are the most urgent issues and concerns within the community? 5. How can the community be more effectively engaged in these processes? 6. The last time you required healthcare, where did you go? 7. What was your experience with the quality of care and water, sanitation, and hygiene (WASH) at the facility? 8. What aspects of the experience went well? 9. What could have been done differently to improve your experience? 10. What does quality of care mean to you personally? 11. What are the most pressing concerns for you regarding WASH in the health facility? 12. Do you feel empowered and engaged enough to suggest improvements to the health facility? 13. Please describe what quality of care means to you in your own words. 14. What motivates you to use the services provided at this facility? 15. Do you feel that you can trust the facility and its healthcare providers? 16. Which stakeholders support WASH and quality initiatives in your country? What approaches are being used, and which facilities or districts are involved? 17. What governance structures exist within your organization, and how do they align with national and local government priorities? 18. To whom is the health center management accountable? 19. Does your organization provide financial support for WASH and/or quality improvement initiatives? 20. What are your reporting lines for the work you do to support national programs? 21. Is there flexibility to interview other key stakeholders, such as those involved in national health insurance or external evaluation bodies, depending on the context? 22. What are the barriers to achieving quality care in health facilities? 23. What practical steps can be taken to ensure universal access to quality care through improved WASH services? 24. How do WASH services contribute to achieving universal health coverage, with examples from countries like Ethiopia, Cambodia, and others? 25. What lessons can be learned from countries that have successfully improved WASH and quality in healthcare facilities? 26. How do national systems support drinking water, sanitation, and hygiene, and what are the global trends in this area? 27. What are the core questions and indicators for monitoring WASH in health facilities within the framework of the Sustainable Development Goals? 28. What methodologies and tools, such as the WASH Facility Improvement Tool (WASH FIT), are available to improve WASH in healthcare settings? 29. How can qualitative research methods, such as expert interviews and content analysis, be applied to better understand and address these issues? 30. What global declarations and frameworks, such as the Declaration of Astana or the Political Declaration on Universal Health Coverage, guide efforts to improve quality care and WASH in health facilities?
